messages.subject: Ploidy number
parts:
Dear Group,
I have a slight problem. I am working with single haploid cells and
genotyping it on human SNP6.0 arrays.
I can run the files and easily make the analysis till copy number
variation.
But I do not know whether I am reading a single allele from my sample
or a heterozygous allele.
As a control I am having an array from same individual with diploid
state.
Is there any way to depict the alleles calls or the ploidy state from
the genotype.
I tried CNV but different SNPs give different value some shows haploid
while others show diploid.
Is there a way to summarize everything and get to know the ploidy
number?
Sincerely
Tarang

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Ploidy number
parts:
Hi,

sorry for the late response. This is not available, but some parts
are in place. What you are asking for requires first of all
allele-specific (AS) estimates. I will only explain that part here.
We haven't made any documentation on this public yet, but the quick
story is that you replace combineAlleles=TRUE with
combineAlleles=FALSE in your PLM summarization, e.g.

plm <- AvgCnPlm(csN, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=FALSE);

and the fit etc. You can then continue with fragment-length
normalization as usual, giving say 'cesN'.

You can then access (thetaA,thetaB) using extractTheta(), e.g.

thetas <- extractTheta(cesN, units=809:934);

and you will see that there is now an additional dimension, which
holds the AS estimates, e.g.

thetaA <- thetas[,1,];
thetaB <- thetas[,2,];

This will give a first way to look at the allele-specific estimates.
Maybe this will help you as a start.

The only this you have to keep in mind for total CN segmentation is
that you "manually" have to add up thetaA and thetaB, which you do by:

as <- AlleleSummation(cesN);
cesT <- process(as, verbose=log);

You can then pass this to the segmentation model (but not cesN), e.g.

cbs <- CbsModel(cesT);

and so on.

/Henrik
